topic.title: Illumination, Reflectance, and Generative Relighting
topic.overview: An image combines lighting, surface properties, and geometry, making their separation ambiguous. This topic studies color constancy, reflectance decomposition, relighting, and geometric inference from specialized visual signals. Recent generative methods can synthesize new lighting conditions without always explicitly estimating every physical component.
topic.whyItMatters: Changing illumination while preserving object identity is useful for editing and scene construction, but plausible appearance alone does not prove physically correct decomposition. Materials such as transparent objects or ice add further ambiguity, motivating measurements and priors tailored to their light-transport behavior.
topic.evolution: A 1987 study learns a linear lightness algorithm from examples in a simplified scene setting. Later work examines color constancy and neural reflectance models. Neural Gaffer in 2024 conditions a diffusion model on environment lighting; recent representatives extend to video and three-dimensional objects, while a 2026 polarization study estimates surface normals in ice using spatial consistency priors.
openQuestions: How can relighting be evaluated separately from changes in material or geometry?
Which physical constraints improve generative editing without restricting its practical range?

papers.title: MMPD-Bench: Bridging Multimodal Fission with Multi-Polarimetric Modalities Decomposition

papers.tldr: DA-SAM combines domain-specific guidance with multidirectional flatness exploration to improve optimization for domain generalization.

papers.tldr: Phy-CoSF reconstructs hyperspectral images through continuous wavelength queries, enabling flexible spectral resolution from snapshot measurements.

papers.title: Plan, Decouple, Assimilate: Physics-Aware Object Insertion in Remote Sensing Imagery
papers.tldr: PDA coordinates placement, illumination, and texture when inserting remote-sensing objects, improving generated-image quality and downstream detection.

papers.title: PolarDepth: Monocular Transparent Object Depth from Polar-Physics Priors
papers.tldr: PolarDepth combines RGB and polarization-derived physical priors to improve depth estimation and localization of transparent objects.

papers.title: Relighting as a Probe of Visual Priors via Augmented Latent Intrinsics
papers.tldr: ALI improves relighting by preserving dense visual cues, revealing a trade-off between semantic abstraction and physical fidelity.

papers.title: Scalable RF Simulation in Generative 4D Worlds

papers.title: Semi-LAR: Semi-supervised Contrastive Learning with Linear Attention for Removal of Nighttime Flares
papers.tldr: Semi-LAR improves nighttime flare removal using refined pseudo-labels and flare-aware contrastive learning on unlabeled images.

papers.tldr: CEN focuses spike cameras by tracking frequency-domain energy shifts, avoiding image reconstruction and handling irregular focus responses.

papers.tldr: SSDCN combines spatial-spectral clustering and hierarchical feature reuse for more efficient, higher-quality hyperspectral super-resolution.

papers.tldr: TransLight separates lighting from reference-image content to enable flexible transfer of structured illumination effects in portrait photography.
